still_true: Wegovy's US list price is still $1,349 a month, and almost nobody pays it.
The FDA has approved no generic semaglutide or tirzepatide in the US; generic liraglutide is still the only generic incretin on the US market.
The TrumpRx cash channel still operates, and oral Wegovy starting doses still cost $149 a month there, with maintenance at $199.
The Medicare GLP-1 Bridge pilot has not been revived, Congress has not reopened the ~$41B CBO-scored permanent benefit, and Medicare still pays for no incretin prescribed for weight loss alone.

The September 2027 tri-agency guidance allowing up to 30% premium differentials tied to verified adherence still stands, Illinois's ban on adherence-conditioned premiums is still the only state ban in force, and the April 2033 Section 232 100% tariff on Chinese and Indian peptide drugs and APIs is still in force.

population.note: FICTIONAL. Cycling arithmetic: 42.4% ever-used − 32.3% current = 10.1% of adults used and are off now; ~54% of current users are on a second or later course (17.4 pts) and 3.0 pts cycled and are off again, so (17.4 + 3.0) / 42.4 ≈ 48.1%; the other 7.1 pts stopped once and have not restarted. Planned 'drug holidays' under 90 days are not counted as stopping. This fits one-year persistence near one-third on cash weekly and oral products (~60% inside conditioned tracks and on clinic MariTide) and ~40–50% restarting within a year, with restarts lifted by the cheap regrown gray market. Age check: 0.20×20.5 + 0.33×32 + 0.24×45 + 0.23×30 = 4.1 + 10.56 + 10.8 + 6.9 ≈ 32.4. Income thirds average 32.3. Users: 32.3% of ~277M adults ≈ 89.5M (up 21.8M). FICTIONAL payer mix: commercial ~17.5M (19.6%, ~10.1M in conditioned tracks); Medicare ~15.5M (17.3%); Medicaid ~4.9M (5.5%, ~1.1M on the AUD label); legitimate cash ~37.0M (41.3%: ~10.5M on 'metabolic health'/longevity plans, ~2.6M calm/focus, ~6.5M indefinite $149 starting dose, ~17.4M ordinary obesity cash); non-approved product ~14.6M (16.3%: ~4.0M 503A 'personalised' compounded, ~6.0M domestically re-filled vials from smuggled API, ~3.5M 'research-grade' powders incl. retatrutide and amycretin analogues, ~1.1M counterfeit/imported pens). Sum 17.5 + 15.5 + 4.9 + 37.0 + 14.6 = 89.5. Non-obese users: ~14M (10.5M legit longevity plans + ~3.5M gray powders), ~5% of adults, concentrated in the top third and ages 40–70. Adult obesity ~31.5%; ~17% of adults have obesity and have never used, still concentrated in the bottom third, the rural South and 65+ without qualifying codes. Pediatric: 2.0% of under-18s, ~3.7% of 12–17s, ~0.7% of 6–11s (~60% of 6–11 starts Medicaid/CHIP under EPSDT); gray powder use by 15–17-year-olds is reported but unmeasured. ~6.1M children live with a parent who has regained after stopping; roughly half of US children now live with at least one current user.

access.public_coverage: No structural change. Medicare (~15.5M users) pays only through diabetes, CV, CKD, OSA, dementia-risk (obesity plus established CVD) and AUD codes, behind prior authorisation. FICTIONAL arithmetic: 15.5M × ~$230 average net/month × 12 ≈ $42.8B gross Part D incretin spend (up from ~$38.3B; growth is volume, since net price stalled). Dementia route ~2.4M × $240 × 12 ≈ $6.9B; AUD route ~1.0M × $205 × 12 ≈ $2.5B. CMS's AUD coding audit closed in 2036 with ~$310M in plan recoupments and tighter AUDIT-C documentation rules, not a coverage change. Medicaid (~4.9M) covers the AUD label in every state under existing rebate law and 6–11s under EPSDT; the same 7 states cover adult weight-loss use; two state programmes still condition coverage.
access.generic_rest_of_world: Indian generic semaglutide still $4–30 a month in India and 100+ export markets; Chinese tirzepatide- and retatrutide-analogue powders $15–50 where patents are not enforced. Canadian and Brazilian generics unchanged at CAD 45–80 and BRL 160–280. Delivered legally to US addresses the tariff still makes them ~$90–180, but transshipped API via Mexico and the UAE now reaches domestic re-fillers and 'research peptide' sellers cheaply enough to retail at $50–120.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Prices stalled: no branded US net or cash price moved more than ±2% in 2035–36. TrumpRx Wegovy pill $149 start / $199 maintenance; Foundayo $149–229; injectable Wegovy/Zepbound $249–299; MariTide $249 direct (~6.5M users); retatrutide ~$399; oral amycretin still ~$449 cash with no TrumpRx price and on allocation since Feb 2035 (~4.5M users, waitlists at most telehealth platforms) because an oral peptide needs dozens of times the API per patient-month of a weekly injection. Business Group on Health (Nov 2036): still 33% of employers cover weight management, ~two-thirds with adherence/progress conditions; ~10.1M in tracks. The gray market regrew from 5.8M to ~14.6M users: a 2035 federal ruling left 503A 'personalised' blends (semaglutide or tirzepatide plus B6, glycine or L-carnitine) sold via telehealth at $129–199; domestic re-fill operations moved from back rooms to licensed-looking 'wellness pharmacies'; and research-chemical sites sell lyophilised 'reta', 'cagri' and amycretin-analogue powders for $50–90 'not for human consumption'. Roughly 1 in 6 users now takes non-approved product, up from 1 in 12.

pediatric obesity ages 6–11 (liraglutide incl. generics; weekly semaglutide), with growth-velocity, Tanner and eating-disorder screening language

drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. No new class reached the US market in 2035–36 (next_gen_launch: none). Tirzepatide dementia 60+ without CVD: resubmitted Apr 2035, advisory committee voted 7–6 in Sep 2036 with hip-fracture excess in women 70+ the sticking point; PDUFA extended to Feb 2037. Implants remain in phase 2. Oral retatrutide and an oral MariTide successor are in phase 2 and not filed. Novo's oral amycretin supply expansion (Clayton NC API line) is due 2037. The longevity_wellness driver is realised entirely off-label: no sponsor has filed a 'metabolic health' indication, and no trial in normal-BMI adults is powered for mortality. Global incretin market ~$235B (2036, volume-driven). US branded net prices flat after a decade of 3–5% annual declines.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the leading cause of discontinuation outside tracks. Re-titration nausea after drug holidays is now a routine telehealth complaint; low-dose longevity users report it less.

safety_ledger.effect: Gastroparesis, ileus and bowel obstruction (persistent delayed gastric emptying)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: First MDL bellwether (Jun 2035) returned a defence verdict on persistence after stopping; the second (Feb 2036) a $4.1M plaintiff verdict on failure-to-warn for ileus. GI claims ~44,000. Cohort data still disputed.
Elevated with rapid weight loss; unchanged.
No causal confirmation; absolute risk low. Pleaded alongside EPI.

safety_ledger.effect: Lean mass (muscle) loss and bone-density loss
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Medicare hip-fracture HR ~1.3 after 2+ years, ~1.45 after three or more cycles. DXA data in normal-BMI longevity users are sparse; clinicians assume proportionally greater lean loss but no study has measured it. No new signal.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class warning retained; bimagrumab restricted label unchanged (~210k users).

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Conflicting cohorts; absolute risk very low.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Listed in adverse reactions; no class warning.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No new adult signal through three years of AUD-label use.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', anhedonia)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Nov 2033 FDA study (~7% vs ~3.5%, ~10% on retatrutide) still the best estimate; no new data. Now the most-cited reason for planned holidays. FDA's low-dose observational study began enrolling in 2036; results expected 2038.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: No labelling change. Professional-society guidance on planned pauses (Jun 2036).

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Half to two-thirds regain within 18 months, worse after repeated cycles. Regain after short holidays (<6 weeks) is typically 1–2 kg and reverses on restart.
B12, iron, vitamin D; thiamine in AUD users who keep drinking; low ferritin in adolescent girls. Unchanged.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Annual panel language and thiamine counselling retained.

safety_ledger.effect: Exocrine pancreatic insufficiency after 5+ years of continuous use
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: ~2× incidence after 5+ years of semaglutide; tirzepatide HR ~1.3. EPI claims ~61,000. Novo settled the DOJ civil investigation for $1.1B with a five-year corporate integrity agreement (Mar 2035).
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled on semaglutide and tirzepatide; no further action.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~5 years; effects in children on drug for decades; effects of repeated on/off cycling
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: ~14 years of semaglutide follow-up. No data on indefinite starting-dose use, on years of low-dose use in normal-BMI adults, or on frequent short holidays.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Pediatric bone and growth PMRs continue.

safety_ledger.effect: Compounded / counterfeit / imported product harms (dosing errors, contamination, substitution)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Adverse-event reports tied to non-approved product passed ~46,000. Reconstitution errors with research powders (10× overdoses) drive poison-centre calls back up to ~6× 2025 levels. Two further contamination clusters (~90 infections, 1 death) in Alabama and Texas. Same harm types; no new signal.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA warning letters to ~60 research-peptide sellers and an expanded import alert; the 2035 court ruling limits action against 503A blends. No statute changed; no state acted.

safety_ledger.effect: Growth deceleration, delayed puberty and restrictive eating in children started young
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Height velocity ~0.5–0.6 cm/year below expected persists in prepubertal starters, with partial catch-up after stopping. Swedish ARFID HR ~1.8. Final adult height unknown.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Monitoring language and medication guide; no REMS.

safety_ledger.effect: Alcohol-related harms on the AUD label (dehydration, alcoholic ketoacidosis, aspiration with vomiting during binge drinking)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: ~1 per 2,000 person-years holds in larger ED data; now also seen at restarts after holidays.

food_and_beverage.state: About half of US households have a current user. Snack and confectionery volumes ~15–17% below 2025, sugary drinks ~13%. The 2033 'tariff bounce' in lower-income zips reversed as cheap compounded and re-filled product returned. Growth is in 'metabolic' functional lines aimed at normal-weight longevity users: fibre, protein waters, glucose-'friendly' bakery. Mondelez and PepsiCo report flat dollars, falling volume, rising price per gram.

alcohol.state: Spirits volume ~21% below 2025, beer ~14%. Wine is now falling too, because the longevity cohort, the upper-income 45–70 dinner-party buyer, drinks less. Napa reports a second year of bulk-wine surplus. Kentucky bourbon employment is down another ~900 jobs. Non-alcoholic drinks are ~6% of category dollars.

restaurants.state: Traffic is flat and checks are smaller. Tasting menus in Austin and Scottsdale sell 'holiday menus' for diners on a planned week off, the first occasion in a decade built around more appetite. Bar revenue in mid-sized Midwestern cities is still falling.

apparel.state: Plus-size keeps shrinking. Normal-weight longevity users dropping one size feed the premium basics refresh. Size-up returns in Memphis-area mass retail eased as gray users restarted.

fitness.state: Strength training grows. Longevity clinics bundle DXA, VO2-max and resistance coaching with low-dose plans. Track InBody scans keep budget chains full.

insurance.state: No structural change. Pharmacy trend ~+6%, all volume. Track vendors added 'clinician-approved pause' codes in 2036 so planned holidays do not cost a premium tier. Unapproved pauses still do. Part D premiums rose again for 2036. Life insurers added an 'incretin history and current status' underwriting question.

pharma.state: Volume growth with flat price. Novo's oral amycretin is supply-capped and its DOJ matter settled; Lilly leads injectables. Both now lose ~16% of patient-months to compounders and powder sellers, including copies of retatrutide and amycretin. Litigation reserves and the API bottleneck are the stated reasons for no price cuts. Hims-style platforms grow on compounded blends.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: A stable, slightly lean body now reads as normal maintenance, like straight teeth. Visible weight change is what gets read. Regain means you stopped, holiday softness means a planned week off, and fast new thinness in a normal-weight 50-year-old means a longevity plan. The unasked question has moved from 'are you on it?' to 'why are you off?'
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: Muscle and a good DXA report are the upper-tier uniform. In Naples, Scottsdale and north Austin, normal-weight retirees and executives take low-dose pills sold as 'metabolic age' management, and 'off-drug lean' has lost its status as a boast because nobody believes it. In Memphis and the Delta the re-filled vial came back at $70–90 from storefront 'wellness pharmacies'. The 2034 regain is partly reversing, at the price of the contamination risk. Medicaid children still make up most 6–11 starts.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Shared meals stay short and drier, but the planned holiday created a new ritual: the holiday dinner, Thanksgiving or a wedding eaten with appetite after a week off. Bread Alone's 'full table' suppers continue at ~1,100 congregations but draw older members. School-nurse medication logs for 6–11s are routine, and the fight about them has faded.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: App tags for 'calm plan' and 'on AUD treatment' became so common that two major apps dropped them. 'Off' and 'on holiday' are now the disclosures that get noticed. Couples report syncing holidays for anniversaries and trips.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Appetite is treated as a setting. Normal people adjust it, and a strong one is a personal decision to explain, or a sign you cannot pay. The 2034 backlash has thinned. MAHA groups split between anti-pediatric hardliners and influencers who sell 'clean' compounded blends, and the 'hunger tax' complaint faded locally once the cheap vials returned.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: The best estimate is still the 2033 FDA figure, ~7% clinically meaningful anhedonia at maintenance dose vs ~3.5% of controls, ~10% on retatrutide. The low-dose rate is unmeasured, though ~14M normal-BMI longevity users and ~2.6M calm subscribers now take low doses. A 2036 KFF survey finds ~38% of current users have taken at least one planned 'holiday' for flatness, an event or sex, and ~22% have self-reduced a dose without telling a prescriber.
interior_life.framing: It is now a widely shared side effect that people dose around, not a feature. People say 'flat weeks' and 'holiday'. Calm platforms quietly softened 'quiet the noise' to 'find your setting'. Clinicians call it dose-related blunting and write pauses. Unmuted's 'sedative' framing gets less traction now that most of its audience is on something.
interior_life.effect_on_work: Inside ~10.1M track enrolments an approved pause code protects the premium tier; an unlogged pause still drops it, so employees ask prescribers for paperwork before a holiday. HR at call centres and warehouses notices holiday weeks as a short-lived bump in absenteeism and irritability, and some schedule around them. FMCSA guidance still covers on-label AUD only. The two EEOC charges are unresolved.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: 'Holiday' became a genre word: festival promoters in Austin and Nashville sell 'off-week' passes, and stand-up and streaming comedy mine the flat-week/holiday-week swing. Sportsbook handle per account keeps falling in insured suburbs but spikes in identifiable holiday windows around big events.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Couples plan sex, travel and arguments around holidays. Therapists report a new pattern: the partner who seems more alive on a holiday week is asked why they don't stay off, and has no good answer about coverage or weight.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: Normalisation drained the backlash. There were no state bills in 2035 or 2036 sessions, and Congress held no incretin hearing in 2036. The live political fight is a trade fight: the tariff stayed, smuggling routed around it, and Southern sheriffs and county health officers complain about contaminated vials without asking for a statewide policy. 'Sedated electorate' claims still lack turnout evidence.

state.regulatory_posture: Federal, permissive on prescribing, overmatched on the gray market. No new approvals of classes. FDA sent warning letters to ~60 research-peptide sellers and expanded an import alert, but lost the 2035 Northern District of Texas case over 503A 'personalised' blends and has not appealed to a conclusion. DOJ settled with Novo ($1.1B, corporate integrity agreement). No state acted; Illinois's ban is still the only one.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: None new. The 2027 tri-agency 30% guidance, OPM's FEHB conditions and Medicaid AUD coverage under existing rebate law all continue unchanged.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: Steady and more granular. Smart-bottle logs, PBM fills and now pause codes flow to wellness vendors, so tracks know not just whether you took it but why you stopped. Longevity platforms sell de-identified 'metabolic age' panels to benefit brokers. Life insurers ask about incretin status. Gray users are invisible to all of it.
state.workforce_or_military: TRICARE covers the AUD label; the Army recruit oral pilot continues unexpanded. Military health officials warned in 2036 that service members are buying research powders off-base.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: The Section 232 tariff and India's export-licence checks stand. Chinese API now reaches US re-fillers and powder sellers through Mexican and UAE transshipment, which CBP has not stopped. Beijing's WTO complaint is in panel. Oral peptides' heavy API demand makes Novo's Danish and North Carolina capacity, and Lilly's US plants, the binding constraint on legitimate supply.

events.event: Novo and Lilly hold 2035 US cash and net prices flat, ending a decade of annual cuts, and Novo places oral amycretin on allocation, saying the pill needs dozens of times more API per patient than an injection; waitlists form at major telehealth platforms

National primary-care membership chains and telehealth platforms launch 'metabolic health' tiers prescribing low-dose Wegovy pill or Foundayo off-label to adults with BMI under 30; legitimate longevity subscribers pass 10 million by late 2036, mostly aged 45–70 in the top income third

A federal judge in the Northern District of Texas declines to enjoin 503A pharmacies' 'personalised' semaglutide and tirzepatide blends, calling FDA's 'essentially a copy' guidance non-binding; compounded telehealth plans relaunch at $129–199 as research-peptide sites sell retatrutide and amycretin-analogue powders built on transshipped Chinese API, and non-approved users reach ~14.6 million

Pew survey finds 61% of upper-income adults under 65 say a friend stopping an incretin 'would need a reason'; two large dating apps drop 'calm plan' tags as too common and life insurers add an incretin-status underwriting question

The Obesity Medicine Association and ACP publish guidance on planned dose pauses for blunting, events and travel; the largest track vendors add a 'clinician-approved pause' code, and FDA begins enrolling a low-dose anhedonia study

FDA advisers split 7–6 on extending tirzepatide's dementia label to over-60s without heart disease, citing hip fractures in women over 70; the decision slips to February 2037, and no state legislature passed an incretin bill in either 2035 or 2036

open_tensions: About 14 million normal-weight adults take incretins for 'metabolic age' with no mortality trial, no lean-mass data in their BMI range and an unmeasured low-dose anhedonia rate. A Medicare dementia extension decision in Feb 2037 could turn part of that cash cohort into a public bill.

One user in six is on non-approved product. A federal court shields 503A blends and transshipment defeats the tariff, so the Southern contamination clusters and powder overdoses have no regulator with both authority and reach.
Flat prices and the oral amycretin bottleneck mean the newest pill rations by waitlist and cash while copies of it sell as research powder. The price stall is what is feeding the gray market.

Drug holidays are now clinically blessed, but tracks punish pauses not coded in advance. Cycling through holidays piles up exposure on bone and pancreas risks that are still poorly characterised for repeated on/off use.

prose.headline: One in three Americans is on it, and the only question anyone asks is why you stopped
prose.world_in_600_words:
At the end of 2036 about ninety million American adults, close to one in three, take an incretin drug, and it has stopped being news. More than four in ten have tried one. The new users of the past two years are mostly not people with obesity. They are fifty-five-year-olds in Scottsdale and north Austin with a body-mass index of twenty-five, who joined a primary-care membership or a telehealth platform offering a 'metabolic health' tier. For about two hundred dollars a month they get a low-dose Wegovy pill or Foundayo, written off-label, plus a blood panel and a scan. Nobody has filed for that indication and no trial has measured whether it lengthens a life. Ten million people subscribe anyway.

The prices did not move. In early 2035 Novo and Lilly held their cash and net prices flat for the first time in a decade. Both cited litigation and, for Novo, the arithmetic of oral peptides: a daily pill needs dozens of times the active ingredient of a weekly shot. Oral amycretin, the pill that matches tirzepatide, is still about $449 a month and is rationed by waitlist. The TrumpRx starting pill is still $149. Who pays has not changed. Medicare still covers nothing for weight alone. A third of employers cover the drugs, and most of them still require proof that you take them.

The gap between the price and the demand was filled the old way. In September 2035 a federal judge in Texas declined to stop pharmacies selling 'personalised' semaglutide and tirzepatide blends, and telehealth compounding came back. Chinese powder now reaches the United States through Mexico and the Emirates despite the tariff. It gets refilled into vials in storefront 'wellness pharmacies' in Memphis, or sold online as research-grade retatrutide for under ninety dollars a month. About one user in six takes something no regulator approved. In the Delta, where the 2033 tariff caused a visible wave of regain, people restarted. Poison-centre calls about reconstitution errors are rising, and two more contamination clusters killed one person. FDA sends letters.

There is no new safety signal. The pancreatic findings, the hip fractures in older women and the slower growth in children are the same as two years ago. The first gastroparesis bellwether ended in a defence verdict and the second in a plaintiff win. Novo settled with the Justice Department for $1.1 billion and is still growing.

What changed is the talk. The flatness clinicians call blunting is now an ordinary complaint, the way people once complained about statin muscle aches. People take holidays from the drug: a week off for a wedding, a festival or an anniversary. In June the obesity physicians published guidance on doing it safely. The wellness vendors that run employer tracks added a code for a clinician-approved pause so that a planned week off does not cost a family its premium tier. An unplanned pause still does. Nearly four in ten users have taken a holiday, and one in five has cut a dose without telling anyone.

Being on the drug is unremarkable, and being off it is what needs explaining. Life insurers now ask. Two dating apps dropped their 'calm plan' tag because everyone had it. The 2034 backlash, which filled the Mall, has thinned, because most of its audience is now taking something. No state passed a bill in 2035 or 2036. Wine is now falling along with spirits, as the longevity cohort drinks less at dinner parties. Snack makers sell less food for more money. In Austin, restaurants offer a 'holiday menu' for diners on a week off. It is the first meal in ten years designed for people who are hungry.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Tomás Ortega wakes in Mesa at six and does not take the pill. Day four. The app shows a small grey suitcase where the green check usually goes: Pause, approved by Dr. Halvorsen, resume Monday.

The coffee tastes like something. He stands at the counter longer than he needs to.

Lorena is at the kitchen table with the vial from Laredo, the one labelled RESEARCH USE ONLY, drawing bacteriostatic water into it with the insulin syringe. She taps it the way the forum video showed her. Eighty-five dollars. 'Don't look at me like that,' she says. 'You teach chemistry. Check my math.' He checks it. It's right.

Third period, the sophomores are balancing equations. In the staff room, Mrs. Pruitt watches him eat the whole burrito.

'You off?'

'Holiday.'

She nods, satisfied, and goes back to her yogurt.

After school his son Mateo, fifteen, is waiting in the car. 'Isaac's on the pink one now. His mom gets it from the place on Main.' Tomás says they'll talk about it. Mateo says that's what he said last time.

At dinner Tomás has seconds and Lorena raises an eyebrow, half amused. Later they watch a comedian do ten minutes on flat weeks, and Tomás laughs hard, from the stomach, and notices himself laughing. Lorena is smiling at the screen, not at the joke.

In bed she says, 'You're louder this week.'

'Is that bad?'

She doesn't answer. His phone lights up on the nightstand: Three days until you resume. You're doing great.
